Re: Appeal of prior-authorization denial  
Requested service: Hip arthroscopy  
CPT: 29914  
Reference number: POC-D304BE9399-97960  
Denial notice date: August 24, 2026  

To Cigna Appeals:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914. The denial states that the submitted records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment. The clinical record does document extensive, provider-directed conservative treatment that was unsuccessful.

The relevant treatment history is:

- I have had 18 months of progressive hip pain that has not improved with rest.
- I used NSAIDs for six months, with inadequate relief.
- I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization, together with activity modification. The treatment occurred from March 28, 2026, through July 4, 2026, and included 16 completed visits. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on April 26, 2026. It provided only two weeks of partial relief, followed by recurrence of symptoms.

The records also establish an objective structural cause for the persistent symptoms. The July 23, 2026 MRI arthrogram showed an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees. The joint space is preserved, and the Tönnis grade is 0.

My symptoms and examination further support the requested procedure. I have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, cannot run or squat, and have positive provocative testing on the affected side. Hip range of motion is limited by pain.

These facts address the specific reason given for denial: conservative treatment was not merely attempted; it was completed over a substantial period and included supervised physical therapy, activity modification, NSAIDs, rest, and injection treatment. These measures failed to provide durable relief. The injection produced only temporary partial benefit, and the symptoms remain functionally limiting.

The record also documents the absence of complicating conditions that would otherwise explain or preclude the requested treatment. There is no active infection or untreated substance use disorder. I am a nonsmoker, and my BMI is 29.

I request that Cigna overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914, based on the complete clinical record. Please have the appeal reviewed by a clinician who was not involved in the initial determination.

For clarity, I am not reproducing or attributing unverified policy language in this letter. Please provide, with the appeal determination, the complete medical-necessity criteria and clinical-review rationale applied to this request, including the specific reason Cigna concluded that the documented 14-week supervised physical-therapy course, activity modification, six months of NSAID treatment, and injection treatment were inadequate.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and issue the decision within the applicable pre-service medical-necessity appeal timeframe.

Sincerely,

Riley Lawson
